title: Grade 4 Science — Wed, Jun 18
description: Skeletal System — Day 3 of 5: Joints — types and functions
subject: science

questions.question: A joint is:
options: The place where two or more bones meet
questions.explanation: A joint is the point where two or more bones meet. Joints allow movement (in moveable joints) or provide strength (in fixed joints).

questions.question: How many main types of joints are there?
questions.explanation: Broadly: moveable joints (allow movement) and immoveable/fixed joints (no movement). Moveable joints include hinge, ball-and-socket, pivot, and gliding types.

questions.question: A HINGE JOINT allows movement:
options: In all directions like a ball
In one direction only — like opening and closing a door
questions.explanation: A hinge joint moves in one plane (like a door hinge). Bending and straightening only. Found at the elbow and knee.

questions.question: Examples of hinge joints are:
questions.explanation: The knee and elbow are classic hinge joints — they bend and straighten in one direction.

questions.question: A BALL-AND-SOCKET joint allows movement:
options: In all directions (forward, backward, sideways, rotation)
questions.explanation: Ball-and-socket joints allow the greatest range of motion — in all directions. The ball (round end of one bone) fits into a socket (cup) of another.

questions.question: Examples of ball-and-socket joints are:
questions.explanation: The shoulder and hip are ball-and-socket joints. You can swing your arm and leg in wide circles — that is ball-and-socket movement.

questions.question: A PIVOT JOINT allows:
questions.explanation: Pivot joints allow rotation. The joint between the first and second vertebrae of the neck is a pivot joint — it lets you shake your head 'no'.

questions.question: Which action uses a pivot joint?
options: Moving your hip in a circle
Shaking your head side to side ('no')
questions.explanation: Shaking your head 'no' (side to side) uses the pivot joint between the atlas (C1) and axis (C2) vertebrae in the neck.

questions.question: FIXED (IMMOVEABLE) joints are joints that:
options: Allow only one direction of movement
Allow no movement — bones are locked together
questions.explanation: Fixed joints (synarthroses) allow no movement. They join bones firmly for protection. The skull's joints are fixed — the bones are fused.

questions.question: The joints in the skull (cranium) are:
questions.explanation: The bones of the skull are joined by immoveable joints called sutures. They protect the brain by holding the skull firmly together.

questions.question: Cartilage at joints acts as a:
options: Cushion (shock absorber) that reduces friction between bones
questions.explanation: Cartilage covers the ends of bones at joints, acting as a shock absorber and reducing friction so bones don't grind against each other.

questions.question: Ligaments are:
options: Tough, flexible bands that connect bone to bone at joints
questions.explanation: Ligaments are tough, flexible connective tissues that hold bones together at joints. They prevent excessive movement and dislocation.

questions.question: Which of these actions uses a BALL-AND-SOCKET joint?
options: Rotating your shoulder to throw a cricket ball
questions.explanation: Throwing a cricket ball involves rotating the shoulder in wide arcs — a ball-and-socket movement.

questions.question: Why do elderly people sometimes have stiff or painful joints?
options: Cartilage wears down over time, causing friction and pain (arthritis)
questions.explanation: With age, cartilage at joints can wear down, causing bones to rub together. This leads to arthritis — pain and stiffness in joints.

questions.question: Which joint type gives you the GREATEST range of movement?
questions.explanation: Ball-and-socket joints (shoulder, hip) provide movement in all directions — the greatest range of any joint type.
